specializations.name: Story & Editing
specializations.inputs: Convert subject matter into a coherent, engaging short-form viewing sequence. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Resolve what viewers must understand, feel or notice next. Choose to retain performance, show evidence/context, insert a metaphor, isolate text or change viewpoint from the narrative change. Use Editorial-Reasoning.md to connect those choices; no reference style, transition quota or fixed pacing is required.
specializations.mechanism: Convert subject matter into a coherent, engaging short-form viewing sequence.
specializations.tradeoff: A dramatic hook promises a different subject than the actual explanation.
specializations.verification: Play the cut without explanatory commentary and record the understood message, missed beats and redundant shots.
specializations.output: beat map, shot/cut plan, time-coded editorial decisions.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: message hierarchy, audience and intent, hook selection, cold opens, cut selection, talking-head/podcast edit, J/L cuts, jump cuts, visual continuity, pacing, speed ramps where editorially justified, humor timing, retention-focused reveals, chapter beats, repeated motifs, loop design.
specializations.failure: A dramatic hook promises a different subject than the actual explanation.
specializations.recovery: Rewrite the hook or reorder the first explanatory beat; preserve the intended claim.
practice: Assign inserts a role: evidence, context, illustration, counterpoint or atmosphere. Preserve provenance and do not imply that decorative footage proves a factual claim.
Let meaningful expression or gesture complete when appropriate; cutaways can carry a narrative change while the speaker remains a continuity anchor.
Choose a caption-led, performance-led or image-led beat deliberately. Coordinate changes in text, framing and treatment so their combined emphasis serves the same idea.

specializations.name: Animated Subtitles & Captions
specializations.inputs: Deliver accessible, synchronized, legible spoken content with optional expressive emphasis. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Resolve whether text is a complete caption, selected emphasis or an independent text scene. Group meaning before choosing replacement, accumulation or another reveal. Preserve exact language and timing provenance; choose hierarchy and emphasis from semantics rather than styling every word identically. Read Expressive-Text.md and route independent text scenes to Kinetic Typography.
specializations.mechanism: Deliver accessible, synchronized, legible spoken content with optional expressive emphasis.
specializations.tradeoff: Captions are visually impressive but mistimed or incomplete.
specializations.verification: Check approved text, qualifiers, speaker/phrase boundaries and actual speech alignment before claiming sync. Inspect final phrase layout, transient blur/scale, projected bounds and encoded mobile readability. Sampled frames leave timing and audiovisual quality unverified.
specializations.output: Role-labeled caption groups with semantic spans, cue provenance, stable layout anchors and animated bounds
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: transcript cleanup, speech segmentation, word-level cue timing, multi-speaker labels, word highlighting, karaoke timing, punch/scale accents, kinetic phrase captions, bilingual captions, readable line breaking, subtitle collisions and avoidance, intentional pauses.
specializations.failure: An expressive group loses a qualifier, moves its anchor accidentally, obscures a face or finishes revealing too late to read.
specializations.recovery: Correct text/alignment first, then simplify or regroup the composition, restage the block and invalidate only affected cue/layout/render ranges.
practice: Plan the final semantic group and its anchor before staged reveals when stable layout is desired. Allow intentional dynamic reflow with explicit bounds.
Use size, weight, color, spacing, placement or a held state as alternative emphasis channels. Preserve negation and small linking words; avoid effect stacking without a reason.
Keep captions separate from decorative keywords and provide complete captions when required. Use readable phrases when word-by-word replacement would obscure syntax.
Allocate entry, readable state and exit from actual reading and speech needs. Motion blur is not a substitute for a legible hold; do not invent word timestamps.
Keep a coherent local vocabulary while permitting new text roles. A source handwriting style, font, color accent or layout is not a universal preset.

specializations.name: Kinetic Typography & Lyric Scenes
specializations.inputs: Turn language into visual scenes, not merely moving text. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Choose whether language is supporting information or the visual scene. When it becomes the scene, construct relationships among words, space, imagery and meaning. A code-like interface, hand lettering, spatial phrase, diagram or another medium is available if it serves the project; retain the approved semantic mapping and role.
specializations.mechanism: Turn language into visual scenes, not merely moving text.
specializations.tradeoff: The metaphor or deformation destroys readability before the phrase is understood.
specializations.verification: Inspect the complete phrase, meaningful intermediate states, glyph correspondence and actual reading speed. Distinguish decorative syntax from verbatim text. Ensure representation changes do not alter qualifiers or imply a working product.
specializations.output: text-scene plan, references, compositional states, animation timelines.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: morphing glyphs, letter physics, word-to-object transformation, typography as environment, icon/text interplay, lyric sequences, metaphor-based letter behavior, 2D/2.5D/3D title choreography, audio-synchronized typographic transitions.
specializations.failure: The metaphor or deformation destroys readability before the phrase is understood.
specializations.recovery: Hold a readable state, simplify deformation and re-evaluate the entry/exit.
practice: Choose the reading order and complete readable state before choosing letter behavior. Type-on should represent input or reveal intent rather than decorate every sentence.
Preserve correspondence across icon, path and word when it helps meaning; color, position, shape or rhythm may carry the link.
Separate text appearance from camera movement. Prefer a still reading interval when movement competes with understanding; check spacing and line breaks through the whole reveal.
Compose connector words and focal words as one phrase with deliberate scale and spacing; reserve readable states rather than treating all words as independent effects.
Text may alternate with footage or persist over a montage to bridge changing images. Choose continuity or reset by meaning, not a fixed sequence.
For code/interface metaphors, separate text/semantic layers, panel state, internal viewport motion and any filmed screen perspective. A creative visual representation need not be executable code.
Expressive irregularity should be controlled: keep useful local anchors and deterministic variation; do not add frame-random jitter solely to suggest handwriting.

specializations.name: Original Motion B-roll & Explainers
specializations.inputs: Build inserted visual sequences that replace or alternate with primary footage to explain meaning. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: A complete cutaway is preferable when adding more overlays would obstruct the subject, overload the scene, or limit explanation.
specializations.mechanism: Build inserted visual sequences that replace or alternate with primary footage to explain meaning.
specializations.tradeoff: The inserted shot is attractive but disconnects the speaker from the argument.
specializations.verification: Play the cutaway in its editorial context and explain the information it adds.
specializations.output: self-contained visual shot with start/end editorial handoffs.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: concept-to-scene metaphors, animated diagrams, timelines, process visualization, comparison scenes, photo collage, map/abstract visualizations, procedural illustration, object deconstruction and exploded view, cutaway sequences, information-to-scene transformation.
specializations.failure: The inserted shot is attractive but disconnects the speaker from the argument.
specializations.recovery: Replace the metaphor or shorten the insert; hand the revised duration to the edit.
practice: Declare the insert role and what new meaning it contributes; preserve its source status. Archival context, a metaphor and decorative atmosphere are different claims.
Use the shot, a phrase or another visual invariant to bridge a montage when useful. Do not copy the source montage order as a universal structure.

specializations.name: Motion Graphics, Cards, Icons & UI
specializations.inputs: Supply concise context and explanations while preserving the main footage's identity. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Choose whether information needs a card, a standalone product view or an interface interaction. Route interdependent UI states to UI Choreography. Preserve recognizable marks and accurate claims; distinguish a stylized demo from demonstrated product capability.
specializations.mechanism: Supply concise context and explanations while preserving the main footage's identity.
specializations.tradeoff: A card obscures the subject or a simulated UI implies an unsupported feature.
specializations.verification: Check each information-bearing bound and factual label in actual composited frames.
specializations.output: responsive, parameterized, reusable visual components with critical-content bounds.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by visual study; source observations do not establish perceptual causality or validated rendering. Verify in the active project.
specializations.capabilities: explain cards, lower thirds, animated logos and service icons, brand icon motion (Instagram, Facebook, ChatGPT, Claude, etc.), callouts and labels, annotated arrows/doodles, interface simulations, app/browser panels, graphs, polls, lists, notifications, CTAs, comparisons.
specializations.failure: A card obscures the subject or a simulated UI implies an unsupported feature.
specializations.recovery: Recompose or use a standalone insert; correct UI content before animation.
practice: Separate component structure, state, interaction and optical treatment; preserve stable IDs across panel changes.
Use measured text bounds, corner radius, stroke width and anchor relationships at final scale. Treat inner content and outer panel transforms separately.
Route focus priorities to Attention Direction and shared motion dependencies to Motion Choreography.

specializations.name: Character & Illustration Animation
specializations.inputs: Use animated characters or illustrations to demonstrate, react, and narrate ideas. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Does character action provide clarity, personality, or humor? Integrate with captions and speaking footage rather than competing for attention.
specializations.mechanism: Use animated characters or illustrations to demonstrate, react, and narrate ideas.
specializations.tradeoff: The character competes with the speaker or changes identity across cuts.
specializations.verification: Review acting, contact, identity and captions together at target speed.
specializations.output: character shot/insertion with rig controls, cues, framing, and review conditions. **Preserve existing character-animation work in Motion; this domain is an editorial integration point, not a replacement.**
specializations.evidence: Authored editorial mechanism; confirm against actual project footage, audio and playback.
specializations.capabilities: rigged pose and motion, gestures, facial expression, eye line, simple lip-sync, reaction inserts, pointer behavior, character/graphic interaction, secondary motion, illustrated scene transitions, consistent visual identity.
specializations.failure: The character competes with the speaker or changes identity across cuts.
specializations.recovery: Restage the reaction and reuse the canonical character; recheck affected rig/performance tracks.

specializations.name: Freeze Frames, Subject Effects & Tracking
specializations.inputs: Make filmed people and objects interact with graphics in an intentional, convincing way. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Which visible subject or object is emphasized, and does tracking hold across movement and occlusion?
specializations.mechanism: Make filmed people and objects interact with graphics in an intentional, convincing way.
specializations.tradeoff: A mask leaks or a tethered label jumps to the wrong object.
specializations.verification: Scrub masks and tracked anchors across occlusion, scale change and re-entry.
specializations.output: keyed/tracked shot with stable masks and subject-safe placement.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: freeze-frame captures, snapshot emphasis, cutout and bold-outline effects, background blur/dim, spotlight, masks and rotoscoping, subject/object tracking, tethered callouts, tracked stickers, parallax from a still, limited subject duplication, foreground occlusion.
specializations.failure: A mask leaks or a tethered label jumps to the wrong object.
specializations.recovery: Use confidence-aware gaps and manual anchors; change the effect if reliable tracking cannot be obtained.
practice: For graphics attached to a filmed display, carry its source-to-output perspective and occlusion separately from motion inside the display. Keep tracking confidence explicit.
A picture may resemble projected type without establishing real 3D construction. Select a simpler native 2D/2.5D or tracked method when it provides the intended result.

specializations.name: Camera, Zoom & Transition Language
specializations.inputs: Direct viewer attention and connect scenes through comprehensible movement. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Is movement serving a reveal, emphasis, spatial continuity, or scene change? Maintain focal continuity and avoid accidental crop of subjects/text.
specializations.mechanism: Direct viewer attention and connect scenes through comprehensible movement.
specializations.tradeoff: Camera movement cuts off protected text or produces an unintended spatial jump.
specializations.verification: Inspect maximal crops and transition boundary frames while following the same subject.
specializations.output: movement trajectories and shot transitions with entry/exit states.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: punch-in/out, digital crop/zoom, push/pull, pan, orbit, whip pan, crash zoom, zoom-through, parallax, camera-roll, subject reframe, transition matching by direction/shape/color/sound, restrained portal entry as a transition option.
specializations.failure: Camera movement cuts off protected text or produces an unintended spatial jump.
specializations.recovery: Modify framing and incoming/outgoing states together; rerun layout checks.
practice: Declare whether a visible change comes from a camera, a group transform or internal object motion; judge the screen result without pretending the source technique is known.
Choose a focal anchor and protect it across pan, scale and the next shot. Recompute text bounds during the full movement.
Coordinate the handoff with Attention Direction and Motion Choreography. Fast zoom, slow drift and a static view are equally valid when appropriate.
Separate outer frame, inset footage and text coordinates through aspect/crop changes. Caption anchors may remain in screen space or move with the footage by design.
Coordinate reframing with emphasis, gesture and readable states. A push-in is an option; rapid zooming or simulated depth is not required for impact.

specializations.name: Color Grading & Visual Look
specializations.inputs: Preserve visible quality while giving footage and graphics a consistent emotional character. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Interpret the source first, correct exposure/balance where needed, match only the relationships that need continuity, then choose the creative look and output treatment. Protect meaningful skin/product information and overlay contrast. Distinct footage roles may deliberately retain different looks; do not apply an inferred LUT from a finished example.
specializations.mechanism: Preserve visible quality while giving footage and graphics a consistent emotional character.
specializations.tradeoff: An intended look crushes detail or makes graphics conflict with footage.
specializations.verification: Compare adjacent shots, representative skin/product detail, shadow/highlight separation, saturation, gradients and actual caption/background combinations after output conversion. Record qualitative source observations separately from measured settings or a verified color pipeline.
specializations.output: shot-matched correction and look parameters tested in the rendered output.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: exposure and white balance correction, matching sources, skin-tone preservation, contrast and tonal hierarchy, selective color, vibrant/soft/cinematic/horror/nostalgic looks, restrained grain/glow, light accents, intentional scene-to-scene look changes, display-safe output transforms.
specializations.failure: An intended look crushes detail or makes graphics conflict with footage.
specializations.recovery: Separate source correction from the creative look; retest the output conversion.
practice: Use value separation and warm/cool relationships as adjustable choices. Keep exact hues, contrast curves, saturation and texture in the project.
Separate overlay rendering from the footage grade; verify any global post-treatment also applied to text. Moving backgrounds can defeat a contrast check made on one still.
Declare scoped grayscale, wash, glow or archival differences when they serve a beat. Preserve context rather than making every source cosmetically identical.
Do not attribute a look to grading alone: lighting, capture, set, wardrobe and compression may contribute. The visible export cannot establish the original log profile or numeric correction.

specializations.name: Sound, Voice & Musical Synchronization
specializations.inputs: Make speech understandable and audio support the visual timing. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Prioritize understandable dialogue. Let music and SFX reinforce—not obscure—the content. Use permitted/licensed sources and avoid implied voice identity without authorization.
specializations.mechanism: Make speech understandable and audio support the visual timing.
specializations.tradeoff: Beat matching cuts a meaningful phrase or masks a key word.
specializations.verification: Listen to speech over music/SFX at ordinary playback level and compare early/late sync cues.
specializations.output: synchronized audio stems/cue map and monitored final mix.
specializations.evidence: Authored editorial mechanism; confirm against actual project footage, audio and playback.
specializations.capabilities: voice cleanup, leveling, ducking, noise reduction, narration/AI voice when available and authorized, music cut and beat mapping, Foley, whoosh/impact/riser design, silence, spatial impression, transition sounds, caption/voice timing, loudness and clipping inspection.
specializations.failure: Beat matching cuts a meaningful phrase or masks a key word.
specializations.recovery: Prioritize phrase semantics, reduce competing sound and move cues using the shared timebase.

specializations.name: Social-Scale Creative VFX & 2.5D
specializations.inputs: Offer expressive transformations within an achievable short-form production budget. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Prefer clear 2D/2.5D illusions over full photorealistic simulation when the latter does not improve the message. Require a visual reference and performance budget for complex sequences.
specializations.mechanism: Offer expressive transformations within an achievable short-form production budget.
specializations.tradeoff: A complex simulation is too slow or visually hides the concept.
specializations.verification: Render the most expensive effect interval and inspect meaning, artifacts and measured cost.
specializations.output: self-contained composited shot with an achievable renderer plan.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by visual study; source observations do not establish perceptual causality or validated rendering. Verify in the active project.
specializations.capabilities: particles, glow, glass and reflection accents, kaleidoscope/mirror scenes, simple portal transitions, planar perspective tricks, liquid/dissolve typography, object assembly/disassembly, collage depth, procedural patterns, motion trails, selective distortions.
specializations.failure: A complex simulation is too slow or visually hides the concept.
specializations.recovery: Replace it with an explicit 2D/2.5D construction or simplify the shot while preserving the meaning.
practice: Define the information carried by a trail, glow, mask or depth illusion before choosing its appearance.
For animated paths coordinate curve trim, taper, travel and emission through existing geometry, transform and compositing owners.
Separate source observations from renderer hypotheses; test an achievable interval before committing to an expensive effect.

specializations.name: Social Composition & Adaptive Safe Zones
specializations.inputs: Keep the design effective across Instagram/Facebook Reels and Stories, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and supported ad placements. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Classify elements as `protected`, `flexible`, `decorative`, or `full_bleed`. Protect information-bearing regions within flexible elements, not the entire container. Recompose layouts when the platform changes rather than blindly scaling.
specializations.mechanism: Keep the design effective across Instagram/Facebook Reels and Stories, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and supported ad placements.
specializations.tradeoff: A caption fits one layout but is hidden in another surface.
specializations.verification: Test protected content against time-varying UI masks at reading holds for every target placement.
specializations.output: per-placement layout profile, time-dependent critical bounds, and preview QA results.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.
specializations.capabilities: subject-aware framing, UI-aware layout, safe-area envelopes, subtitle clearance, priority-based occlusion, portrait/landscape/square adaptation, optical alignment, negative space, intentional overflow, device previews, time-varying layout collision testing.
specializations.failure: A caption fits one layout but is hidden in another surface.
specializations.recovery: Recompose the placement variant; do not blindly shrink all scene contents.
practice: Treat baked black margins, rounded picture windows and source framing as separate from platform UI clearance. Define protected text/face/action regions from the current output.
Evaluate actual background changes, phrase expansion and camera extremes. Recompose per variant and language rather than blindly transferring one word index or scaling a source layout.

specializations.name: Opening, Ending & Cover Design
specializations.inputs: Establish a compelling first impression and meaningful conclusion. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Choose an opening according to audience and story; avoid an intro that delays the content's purpose.
specializations.mechanism: Establish a compelling first impression and meaningful conclusion.
specializations.tradeoff: An intro delays the message or the cover promises content absent from the edit.
specializations.verification: Review opening, ending and selected cover crops independently and in sequence.
specializations.output: opening/ending sequences and cover candidates linked to the editorial timeline.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by visual study; source observations do not establish perceptual causality or validated rendering. Verify in the active project.
specializations.capabilities: cold opens, hook shots, title treatments, cinematic but short intros, contextual logo appearances, chapter reveals, visual punchline, outros, seamless loops, end cards, creator identity, cover/thumbnail frames, feed preview and crop.
specializations.failure: An intro delays the message or the cover promises content absent from the edit.
specializations.recovery: Move identity treatment into the content; choose a truthful cover and purposeful ending.
practice: Use identity motion to establish or resolve the story when it serves the brief. Keep mark geometry and wordmark spacing recognizable through entry and settle.
Design the final relationship between mark, name and empty space; keep the end readable before any exit.
A point-to-symbol, draw-on, assembly, direct cut or quiet wordmark are options; do not impose a signature logo reveal on every project.

specializations.name: Production, Platform Delivery & Quality
specializations.inputs: Deliver technically valid, visually legible social video and source materials. Inputs come from the shared project contracts and connected technical owners.
specializations.decision: Generate platform-specific outputs only when the surface differs materially. Verify actual files and final frames before describing production as complete.
specializations.mechanism: Deliver technically valid, visually legible social video and source materials.
specializations.tradeoff: A valid encode contains stale frames, wrong captions or an unverified placement crop.
specializations.verification: Fully decode exports, inspect A/V metadata and watch target-sized playback with the actual caption/audio mix.
specializations.output: verified export variants and repeatable source-build package.
specializations.evidence: Authored editorial mechanism; confirm against actual project footage, audio and playback.
specializations.capabilities: reference manifest, code-based scene generation, timeline assembly, compositing, format profiles, bitrate/codec/frame-rate decisions, audio/video synchronization, MP4 validation, export variants, poster/cover, file naming, re-rendering, mobile QC, clipping/crop checks, source and license manifest.
specializations.failure: A valid encode contains stale frames, wrong captions or an unverified placement crop.
specializations.recovery: Invalidate the relevant build signature and regenerate affected ranges and variants.
